title: This Primate Knocks on Trees to Find Food Hiding Inside
subject: aye-aye

scenes.text: This primate knocks on trees like a doctor tapping a chest.
It's the aye-aye, the biggest nocturnal primate on Earth, at about four pounds.
It taps up to eight times a second, and listens for echoes.
A hollow echo means a chamber, and chambers hide grubs.
It gnaws a hole, then hooks them out with one thin, bony middle finger.
Scientists call it percussive foraging. Few mammals hunt this way.
